name: Vitamin C and zinc pit routine
lead: The vitamin C and zinc pit routine is an informal underarm-care practice discussed in grooming circles as a way to smell fresher, typically involving topical or dietary vitamin C and zinc. People use it because underarm odor affects how a person comes across up close, and they hope to reduce it without relying only on conventional deodorant or antiperspirant.

Underarm odor arises when bacteria on the skin break down apocrine sweat secretions into odorous compounds; Corynebacterium and Staphylococcus species are among those involved, and genetics, diet and the gut microbiome also influence odor.[1][2] Established approaches include daily washing with antibacterial soap, deodorants that limit bacteria or mask odor, and antiperspirants that reduce sweating.[2][3]
No published study of the vitamin C and zinc routine itself was located; Wikipedia's articles on body odor and deodorants do not mention zinc supplements or vitamin C for odor.[2][3]

paras: Body odor is attributed mainly to skin bacteria acting on apocrine sweat in the armpits, with variation linked to genes such as ABCC11.[1] A common variant that disables the ABCC11 gene reduces underarm odor and is far more common in East Asian populations than in European or African ones.[2] Diet also changes body odor; in one study, men who ate more fruits and vegetables had sweat described as more pleasant.[2]

Deodorants either stop sweat or allow it while limiting the bacteria that break it down. Antiperspirants use aluminium salts, and other products use antibacterial agents, alcohol, charcoal or fragrance.[3] Zinc oxide was among the ingredients in some of the first patented deodorants, along with acids.[3] Acidifying products are described as helping preserve the skin's natural acidity.[3] Manufacturer pages for zinc ricinoleate describe it as a deodorant ingredient, though that is product literature rather than a study.
No studies found of the vitamin C and zinc routine, or of oral vitamin C or zinc supplements for body odor.

card.summary: An anecdotal underarm-odor routine built on vitamin C and zinc, with no studies behind it.
card.note: Anecdotal only; persistent odor may warrant a medical check.

quick.overview:
This routine is an informal approach to underarm odor that people describe using vitamin C and zinc.

The practice is anecdotal and no published trials of it were found.
quick.mechanism: Underarm odor is generally attributed to bacteria breaking down sweat. Proponents of the routine have not had their mechanism tested in published research.
quick.risks: No specific harms are documented for the routine itself. Persistent odor is sometimes linked to medical causes.

chain: Skin bacteria break down underarm sweat into odorous compounds
Routine adds vitamin C and zinc, topically or by mouth
angle.text: Users apply or take vitamin C and zinc hoping for less underarm odor, so they smell fresher at close range. Their expectation is that the ingredients reduce odor-producing activity.
